title: Rigveda 5.65: To Mitra and Varuna
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 5.65: To Mitra and Varuna: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 5.65 is a hymn of 6 verses addressed to Mitra and Varuna. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 5, the family book of the Atri clan. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 385r-385v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 5.65.1-3 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 4, varga 3); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 385r
translation.original_text:
1yaś ci̱keta̱ sa su̱kratu̍r deva̱trā sa bra̍vītu naḥ | varu̍ṇo̱ yasya̍ darśa̱to mi̱tro vā̱ vana̍te̱ gira̍ḥ ||
2tā hi śreṣṭha̍varcasā̱ rājā̍nā dīrgha̱śrutta̍mā | tā satpa̍tī ṛtā̱vṛdha̍ ṛ̱tāvā̍nā̱ jane̍-jane ||
3tā vā̍m iyā̱no 'va̍se̱ pūrvā̱ upa̍ bruve̱ sacā̍ | svaśvā̍sa̱ḥ su ce̱tunā̱ vājā̍m̐ a̱bhi pra dā̱vane̍ ||
translation.text:
1FULL wise is he who hath discerned: let him speak to us of the Gods,– The man whose praise-songs Varuṇa the beautiful, or Mitra, loves.
2For they are Kings of noblest might, of glorious fame most widely spread; Lords of the brave, who strengthen Law, the Holy Ones with every race.
3Approaching you with prayer for aid, together I address you first We who have good steeds call on you, Most Sage, to give us strength besides.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 385r (numbered 58r by the scribe) (OPenn image 385, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.64.6 ‹-vāja-sātaye kṛtam rāye svastaye›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 385v (numbered 58v by the scribe), begins in RV 5.65.4 ‹gātum vanate mitrasya hi›. Verses 5.65.1-3 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1yaḥ | ciketa | saḥ | su-kratuḥ | deva-trā | saḥ | bravītu | naḥ | varuṇaḥ | yasya | darśataḥ | mitraḥ | vā | vanate | giraḥ
2tā | hi | śreṣṭha-varcasā | rājānā | dīrghaśrut-tamā | tā | satpatī itisat-patī | ṛta-vṛdhā | ṛta-vānā | jane--jane
3tā | vām | iyānaḥ | avase | pūrvau | upa | bruve | sacā | su-aśvāsaḥ | su | cetunā | vājān | abhi | pra | dāvane

translation.original_ref: RV 5.65.4-6 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 4, varga 3); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 385v
translation.original_text:
4mi̱tro a̱ṁhoś ci̱d ād u̱ru kṣayā̍ya gā̱tuṁ va̍nate | mi̱trasya̱ hi pra̱tūrva̍taḥ suma̱tir asti̍ vidha̱taḥ ||
5va̱yam mi̱trasyāva̍si̱ syāma̍ sa̱pratha̍stame | a̱ne̱hasa̱s tvota̍yaḥ sa̱trā varu̍ṇaśeṣasaḥ ||
6yu̱vam mi̍tre̱maṁ jana̱ṁ yata̍tha̱ḥ saṁ ca̍ nayathaḥ | mā ma̱ghona̱ḥ pari̍ khyata̱m mo a̱smāka̱m ṛṣī̍ṇāṁ gopī̱the na̍ uruṣyatam ||
translation.text:
4E'en out of misery Mitra gives a way to dwelling at our ease, For he who worships hath the grace of Mitra, fighter in the van. '
5In Mitra's shelter that extends to utmost distance may we dwell, Unmenaced, guarded by thy care, ever as sons of Varuṇa.
6Ye, Mitra, urge this people on, and to one end direct their ways. Neglect not ye the wealthy chiefs, neglect not us the R̥ishis: be our guardians when ye quaff the milk.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 385v (numbered 58v by the scribe) (OPenn image 386, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.65.4 ‹gātum vanate mitrasya hi›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 386r (numbered 59r by the scribe), begins in RV 5.66.2 ‹dhāyi darśatam›. Verses 5.65.4-6 end on this page; 5.65.4 begins on fol. 385r (numbered 58r by the scribe).

4mitraḥ | aṃhoḥ | cit | āt | uru | kṣayāya | gātum | vanate | mitrasya | hi | pra-tūvartaḥ | su-matiḥ | asti | vidhataḥ
5vayam | mitrasya | avasi | syāma | saprathaḥ-tame | anehasaḥ | tvāūtayaḥ | satrā | varuṇa-śeṣasaḥ
6yuvam | mitrā | imam | janam | yatathaḥ | sam | ca | nayathaḥ | mā | maghonaḥ | par i | khyatam | mo iti | asmākam | ṛṣīṇām | go--pīthe | naḥ | uruṣyatam
